wa-whatsapp.note: docs/GRANT-POLICY.md: an explicit requested send (whatsapp_send) may go to any chat - the owner's decision of 06/11 that the new bridge sends ordinary messages freely, like the old connector - under a global cap of 20/min, a per-chat cap of 6/min and a daily cap of 500, with every decision audited. The target is always the exact JID the caller named (chat:<jid>), so the old chat:self / chat:alerts aliases are gone: a status/broadcast or newsletter chat is denied outright, and the automatic paths (transcript posting and the own-chat alert log) keep their own gates (post_transcripts / post_allow / alerts) and are still charged by the global cap on every frame they write. net.dial and http.request mirror the addresses in rust/components/wa-whatsapp/manifest.json; each pattern may only ever NARROW that manifest. kv.write lists the key prefixes rust/components/wa-whatsapp/src/store.rs writes (dev, id/, ses/, pk/, spk/, sk/, sync/, ver/, mac/, lid/, tc/), the transcript prefix tx/ from src/lib.rs, the message fence prefix fence/ from src/guest.rs and the message index prefix ix/ from src/index.rs (records, secondary keys, the token index and the retention age index; docs/SERVICE-COMPONENTS.md, the message index section). credentials.read names the secret the component is given. stt.start is not sensitive (it has no target and no rate): the recognizer itself is granted by the manifest's capabilities.stt, and the empty rule records that this component asks the kernel to run it.

mcp-whatsapp.note: Read tools over the local connector API. Its manifest grants loopback only, so these rules are loopback only; the token is the one its manifest hands it through file_env.

svc-echo.note: Fixture: loopback only, and it writes its own kv namespace. Present so the fixtures of this tree are never refused for want of a rule - the same entry covers the wasip1 module (net only), the wa:kernel@0.1 component and the @0.2 component (net + storage). The wasip1 runner is not policy-checked yet (docs/GRANT-POLICY.md, 'What is not wired yet'); both wasm component contracts are.

svc-echo-v1.note: Fixture on wa:kernel@0.1 (poll contract): the same loopback dial and its own kv namespace as svc-echo, so both component contracts of this tree run under the shipped default without a rule of their own being forgotten.

mcp-echo.note: Fixture: declares no net and no secret, so it needs no rule. It is listed so the file says what the node runs, and so that adding a capability to it is a visible edit here too.

example-new-component.note: TEMPLATE - not a component this tree installs; a policy rule can only narrow a manifest grant, so an entry for a name nothing installs governs nothing. To admit a new component: copy this entry, rename it to the installed name, and keep only the capabilities its manifest declares. A sensitive capability (credentials.read, net.dial, http.request, whatsapp.send, exec.run, kv.write) with NO rule is refused with no_policy once a policy file exists - that is the point of the file. {} means 'any target, no rate'; a non-empty allow list REFUSES a call that has no target. See docs/GRANT-POLICY.md.
